places.name: Ur
places.note: City in Sumer; later capital of the Ur III state. The marker indicates the city, not its territorial reach.

roles.label: Capital of the Ur III state
City under successor southern Mesopotamian states

places.name: Uruk
places.note: Major southern Mesopotamian city. Its political role changed across many periods.

places.name: Kish
places.note: City north of Sumer’s southern centers; one of the early competing dynastic centers.

places.name: Nippur
places.note: Religious center retained by successive southern Mesopotamian rulers.

places.name: Lagash
places.note: Sumerian city and political center in the late third millennium BCE.

places.name: Isin
places.note: A successor dynasty to Ur III and one of the rivals for southern Mesopotamia. These dates mark political prominence, not the city’s full occupation.

places.name: Larsa
places.note: Rival southern Mesopotamian dynasty; its political prominence ended with Hammurabi’s conquest. These dates do not mark the city’s full occupation.

places.name: Babylon
places.note: City and later capital of major Babylonian states; its significance continued beyond this selected display window.

places.name: Ashur
places.note: City on the Tigris and enduring Assyrian religious center; Assyrian political capitals later changed.

places.name: Nineveh
places.note: Assyrian city and capital under Sennacherib in the seventh century BCE.

places.name: Ebla
places.note: Bronze Age Syrian city and kingdom, linked to wider Mesopotamian exchange.

places.name: Hazor
places.note: Canaanite city-state in the southern Levant. The broad window marks selected Bronze and Iron Age relevance.

places.name: Samaria
places.note: Capital of the northern Kingdom of Israel, then center of an Assyrian province after about 722 BCE; later known as Sebaste.

roles.label: Capital of the Kingdom of Israel
Samaria / later Sebaste under changing rulers

places.name: Jerusalem
places.note: Capital of Judah and later a center of Judea. Political control and territorial names changed across this long interval.

roles.label: Capital of the Kingdom of Judah
